title: New Heart Attack Definitions Could Lead to Better Care for Women - Nautilus
gist: Four leading cardiology organizations, including the American College of Cardiology and American Heart Association, agreed on major revisions to the clinical definition of myocardial infarction, announced at the European Society of Cardiology's annual congress, aimed at closing a diagnostic gap that has historically underserved women.

themes.theme: Closing the cardiac diagnostic gender gap

insights.claim: Heart disease is the number one cause of death for women in America, yet myocardial infarctions (heart attacks) in women are frequently mis- or undiagnosed because they present with subtler symptoms — fatigue, nausea, shortness of breath — rather than the classic stabbing chest pain typical in men.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A well-documented diagnostic bias in a leading cause of female mortality represents a persistent unmet clinical need — relevant to diagnostics companies developing sex-specific cardiac biomarkers or symptom-detection tools.

insights.claim: Four of the world's leading heart-health organizations, including the American College of Cardiology and the American Heart Association, agreed on major changes to the clinical definition of myocardial infarction, announced at the European Society of Cardiology's annual congress in Germany.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A coordinated, multi-society redefinition of a core diagnostic criterion is a significant clinical-practice shift that could alter diagnosis rates, billing codes, and clinical trial eligibility criteria tied to MI diagnosis — worth tracking for cardiology-focused healthcare and diagnostics companies.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning "Four of the world’s leading heart health groups"

insights.claim: The updated MI definitions are explicitly framed as targeting 'uncommon heart attack causes' that disproportionately affect women, implying the diagnostic changes are designed to formally recognize female-pattern heart attack presentations.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: If formally codified, broader MI definitions could expand the diagnosed patient population and associated treatment/device markets, particularly benefiting products targeted at women's cardiac care.
insights.locator: subheadline: "Uncommon heart attack causes disproportionately affect them"
